source_refs.note: Book p. 38-39: 3.3.2 Absolute Value Quadratic Inequalities, Example 6 with its two number lines (stops before Exercise 3.1); callouts marked Teaching note / Key points / Common mistake and the Book correction boxes are ours.

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein absolute value wali equation thi, yani "barabar". Ab hum inequality dekhenge, yani "kam" ya "zyada". Yahan jawab ek do number nahi balke poore intervals hote hain. Is ke liye do cheezein chahiye: 3.3 ke absolute value rules, aur quadratic inequality hal karne ka critical-number tareeqa. Dono neeche samjhaye gaye hain.
Absolute value quadratic inequalities aisi inequalities hain jin mein absolute value ki lakeeron ke andar quadratic expression hota hai. Aam tor par yeh in shaklon mein hoti hain:

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehle absolute value ko 3.3 ke rules se aam inequalities mein badlein (yahan \(d > 0\)):
\(|E| < d\) ban jata hai \(-d < E < d\): do inequalities "aur" (and) se juri hui; jawab dono ke hal ka mushtarka hissa (intersection) hai.
\(|E| > d\) ban jata hai \(E < -d\) ya \(E > d\): jawab dono ka majmooa (union) hai.
Phir har quadratic inequality ko critical-number tareeqe se hal karein:
1. Sab kuch ek taraf laayein aur 0 se muqabla karein.
2. "\(= 0\)" wali equation hal kar ke critical numbers nikaalein.
3. Unhein number line par lagayein; yeh line ko hisson (regions) mein baant dete hain.
4. Har hisse se ek point test karein; jahan inequality sach ho woh hissa rakhein.
5. \(<\), \(>\) ke liye kinare khule (open), aur \(\le\), \(\ge\) ke liye band (closed).

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Ek kaam ki baat jo test points ko samajhne mein madad deti hai: agar \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient positive ho (upar khulne wala parabola), to expression apne do roots ke beech negative aur roots ke bahar positive hota hai. Is liye "\(< 0\)" ka jawab roots ke beech wala hissa, aur "\(> 0\)" ka jawab bahar ke do hisse. Example 6 mein bilkul yahi hua: (i) "\(> 0\)" thi to bahar ke hisse aaye, (ii) "\(< 0\)" thi to beech wala hissa. Phir bhi kitab ki tarah har hisse mein ek point zaroor test kijiye; yeh ghalti pakarne ka sab se mehfooz tareeqa hai, khaas tor par jab \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient negative ho.

blocks.title: Example 6
steps:
Given: \(|x^{2} - 6x - 4| < 3\).
To find: tamam real \(x\) jo inequality ko poora karein, intervals ki shakal mein.
Method: sab se pehle absolute value ko hataate hain. \(|E| < 3\) ka matlab \(-3 < E < 3\) hai. Is se do quadratic inequalities, (i) aur (ii), banti hain jo dono ek saath sach honi chahiye. Har ek ko critical numbers (roots) nikaal kar aur har hisse (region) mein ek point test kar ke hal karenge; phir dono ka mushtarka hissa (intersection) lenge.

Step 1: Absolute value hatayein
\[|x^{2} - 6x - 4| < 3\]
\[-3 < x^{2} - 6x - 4 < 3\]
Kyun: jis number ka 0 se faasla 3 se kam ho, woh \(-3\) aur \(3\) ke beech hi hota hai. Yeh 3.3 ka "\(|E| < a\)" wala rule hai.

Step 2: Do inequalities mein torein
\[-3 < x^{2} - 6x - 4\]
\[\text{aur}\quad x^{2} - 6x - 4 < 3\]
Kyun: \(-3 < E < 3\) asal mein do baatein ek saath keh raha hai: "\(-3 < E\)" aur "\(E < 3\)". Dono ka sach hona zaroori hai, is liye jorne wala lafz "aur" (and) hai, "ya" (or) nahi.

Step 3: Sab kuch ek taraf laayein
\[x^{2} - 6x - 4 + 3 > 0\]
\[x^{2} - 6x - 1 > 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
\[x^{2} - 6x - 4 - 3 < 0\]
\[x^{2} - 6x - 7 < 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
Kyun: pehli inequality mein dono taraf 3 jama kiya (is liye \(-3 < E\) ban gaya \(E + 3 > 0\)); doosri mein dono taraf se 3 tafreeq kiya. Jab quadratic ka muqabla 0 se ho to us ke roots hi hadein (boundaries) ban jate hain.

Step 4: (i) ke critical numbers: \(x^{2} - 6x - 1 = 0\)
\[x = \dfrac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^{2} - 4(1)(-1)}}{2(1)}\]
\[x = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 + 4}}{2} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{40}}{2}\]
Kyun: yeh expression integers se factorize nahi hota (product \(-1\) aur sum \(-6\) wale integers nahi milte), is liye quadratic formula: \(a = 1\), \(b = -6\), \(c = -1\).
Dhyan dein: \(-4(1)(-1) = +4\) hai; do minus mil kar plus.

Step 5: Roots ko simplify karein
\[x = \dfrac{6 \pm 2\sqrt{10}}{2} = 3 \pm \sqrt{10}\]
\[x = 3 - \sqrt{10},\quad 3 + \sqrt{10}\]
\[x \approx -0.16,\quad 6.16\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{40} = \sqrt{4 \times 10} = 2\sqrt{10}\), aur \(\sqrt{10} \approx 3.162\). Yeh do critical numbers number line ko teen hisson mein baant dete hain (neeche Figure (i)).

Step 6: (i) ke har hisse mein ek point test karein
\(x = -1\): \((-1)^{2} - 6(-1) - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow 6 > 0\) (True)
\(x = 0\): \((0)^{2} - 6(0) - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow -1 > 0\) (False)
\(x = 7\): \((7)^{2} - 6(7) - 1 > 0 \Rightarrow 6 > 0\) (True)
(i) ka solution set \((-\infty, -0.16) \cup (6.16, \infty)\) hai.
Kyun: quadratic expression ka sign sirf us ke roots par badal sakta hai. Is liye kisi hisse ka ek point jo jawab de, wahi poore hisse ka jawab hai. Yeh graph se bhi samajh aata hai: \(y = x^{2} - 6x - 1\) upar khulne wala parabola hai, jo roots ke bahar positive aur andar negative hota hai.

Step 7: (ii) ke critical numbers: \(x^{2} - 6x - 7 = 0\)
\[x^{2} + x - 7x - 7 = 0\]
\[x(x + 1) - 7(x + 1) = 0\]
\[(x + 1)(x - 7) = 0\]
\[x = -1,\quad x = 7\]
Kyun: humein aise do numbers chahiye jin ka product \(-7\) aur sum \(-6\) ho: yeh \(1\) aur \(-7\) hain. Yeh critical numbers bhi number line ko teen hisson mein baant dete hain (neeche Figure (ii)).

Step 8: (ii) ke har hisse mein ek point test karein
\(x = -2\): \((-2)^{2} - 6(-2) - 7 < 0 \Rightarrow 9 < 0\) (False)
\(x = 0\): \((0)^{2} - 6(0) - 7 < 0 \Rightarrow -7 < 0\) (True)
\(x = 10\): \((10)^{2} - 6(10) - 7 < 0 \Rightarrow 33 < 0\) (False)
(ii) ka solution set \((-1, 7)\) hai.
Kyun: wahi daleel jo Step 6 mein thi. Is dafa "\(< 0\)" hai, is liye roots ke andar wala hissa sach nikla.

Step 9: Mushtarka hissa (intersection) lein
\[\{(-\infty, -0.16) \cup (6.16, \infty)\}\]
\[\cap\ (-1, 7)\]
\[= (-1, -0.16) \cup (6.16, 7)\]
Kyun: (i) aur (ii) dono sach hone chahiye, is liye sirf woh numbers rakhte hain jo dono sets mein hon. Number line par dono figures ko ek doosre ke upar rakh kar dekhiye: dono jagah sach sirf \(-1\) se \(-0.16\) tak aur \(6.16\) se \(7\) tak hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(x = -0.5\) (andar): \(|0.25 + 3 - 4| = 0.75 < 3\). Sahi.
\(x = 6.5\) (andar): \(|42.25 - 39 - 4| = 0.75 < 3\). Sahi.
\(x = 3\) ((ii) mein hai magar (i) mein nahi): \(|9 - 18 - 4| = 13\), jo 3 se kam nahi. Theek hai ke yeh hal mein nahi.
\(x = -1\) (kinara): \(|1 + 6 - 4| = 3\), jo 3 se kam nahi. Is liye kinara shamil nahi (open interval).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab \(-3 < x^{2} - 6x - 4 < 3\) ko "\(-3 < x^{2} - 6x - 4\) or \(x^{2} - 6x - 4 < 3\)" mein torti hai. Yahan "or" nahi, "and" hona chahiye, kyun ke double inequality ka matlab hai ke dono hisse ek saath sach hon. Agar "or" lein to (i) aur (ii) ka union har real number ban jata hai, jo ghalat hai: misaal \(x = 3\) par \(|-13| = 13\), jo 3 se kam nahi. Aakhir mein kitab khud intersection (\(\cap\)) leti hai, jo sahi hai. Hum ne Step 2 mein "aur" likha hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Aakhri line kitab mein na-barabar brackets ke saath chhapi hai: "\((-\infty, -0.16) \cup (6.16, \infty)\} \cap \{(-1, 7) = \ldots\)". Sahi shakal: \(\{(-\infty, -0.16) \cup (6.16, \infty)\} \cap (-1, 7) = (-1, -0.16) \cup (6.16, 7)\). Nateeja khud durust hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: \(-0.16\) aur \(6.16\) asal mein \(3 - \sqrt{10} = -0.1623\ldots\) aur \(3 + \sqrt{10} = 6.1623\ldots\) ki round ki hui values hain. Bilkul durust jawab \((-1,\ 3 - \sqrt{10}) \cup (3 + \sqrt{10},\ 7)\) hai. Exam mein exact shakal aur decimal dono likh dein; is se examiner ko dono taraf ka yaqeen ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar sawal \(|x^{2} - 6x - 4| > 3\) hota (yani "\(>\)") to jawab kya hota? Pehle khud sochiye.
Jawab: ab \(E < -3\) ya \(E > 3\), yani \(x^{2} - 6x - 1 < 0\) ya \(x^{2} - 6x - 7 > 0\). Pehli ka hal \((3 - \sqrt{10},\ 3 + \sqrt{10})\), doosri ka \((-\infty, -1) \cup (7, \infty)\). "Ya" hai, is liye union: \((-\infty, -1) \cup (3 - \sqrt{10},\ 3 + \sqrt{10}) \cup (7, \infty)\). Ghor karein: yeh Example 6 ke jawab ka bilkul baaqi hissa hai (sirf kinare \(-1, 3 \pm \sqrt{10}, 7\) dono mein nahi, kyun ke wahan \(|E| = 3\)).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahi.
(1) \(|x^{2} - 4| \le 5\): \(-5 \le x^{2} - 4 \le 5\). Baen hissa \(x^{2} \ge -1\) har real \(x\) ke liye sach hai. Daen hissa \(x^{2} \le 9\), yani \(-3 \le x \le 3\). Intersection: \([-3, 3]\). Yahan "\(\le\)" hai, is liye kinare shamil (square brackets).
(2) \(|x^{2} - 1| > 3\): \(x^{2} - 1 < -3\) ya \(x^{2} - 1 > 3\). Pehli \(x^{2} < -2\) kabhi sach nahi; doosri \(x^{2} > 4\), yani \(x < -2\) ya \(x > 2\). Jawab: \((-\infty, -2) \cup (2, \infty)\).
Tasdeeq (2): \(x = 3\) par \(|9 - 1| = 8 > 3\), sahi; \(x = 0\) par \(|-1| = 1\), jo 3 se bara nahi, is liye 0 jawab mein nahi. Theek.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(|E| < d \Leftrightarrow -d < E < d\): "aur", intersection.
2. \(|E| > d \Leftrightarrow E < -d\) ya \(E > d\): "ya", union.
3. Har quadratic inequality critical numbers aur test points se hal hoti hai.
4. \(<\), \(>\) ke liye open circles aur gol brackets; \(\le\), \(\ge\) ke liye band kinare aur square brackets.
5. Aakhri jawab ko andar aur bahar ke ek ek point se check karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(|E| < d\) ke liye "or" (union) le lena: yahan "and" (intersection) hai. Kitab bhi beech mein yahi ghalti likh gayi hai.
2. Sirf ek hisse ko test karna: har hissa test karein, kyun ke quadratic ka sign har critical number par badal sakta hai.
3. Strict inequality (\(<\), \(>\)) mein kinare shamil kar lena.
4. Terms ek taraf le jate waqt sign ki ghalti: \(-3 < E\) ban jata hai \(E + 3 > 0\), \(E - 3 > 0\) nahi.
